scope: Private reviewed-application-answer file creation, atomic publication, process interruption and exact-file recovery.
changes: Create temporary answer files with the standard exclusive private-file primitive; POSIX bytes begin at mode 0600.
Request mode 0700 only for newly created scoped directories; preserve existing directory permissions.
Recover only exact expected bytes from a regular file with one hard link; reject final symlink aliases where supported and avoid blocking on special-file open.
Restrict and fsync the matched POSIX file descriptor before recording the recovered document.
Classify file storage failures with fixed safe output and preserve immutable hashes, profile scope and no-store downloads.

verification.environment: isolated Linux container, nonroot UID 10001, network disabled, read-only source
verification.note: Existing runtime image supplies dependencies only; all tested source and tests are mounted from the identified isolated worktree.

verification.environment: isolated native Windows virtual environment with existing installed dependencies
verification.skip_reason: POSIX permission and hard-link semantics; all six selected cases passed in Linux.

baseline_reproduction.observed: Initial write, process death at fsync, and matching uncommitted-file recovery each retained mode 0666 under permissive umask; expected 0600.

production_observation.note: This observation predates deployment of the fix and is not changed-behavior acceptance.

limitations: Full original PII requirement remains incomplete; this slice does not establish all contact/resume/history/session protections.
Native Windows ACL isolation was not tested or changed.
Historical exports and backups are not scanned or rewritten; only new writes and an exact encountered recovery artifact are covered.
No production applicant data, external employer submissions, live AI calls or paid agents were used.
Protected CI, actual candidate merge verification, merge and deployment remain separate pending gates.

claims: No middleware, adapter, database-control, dependency, migration or fleet configuration changes.
Fsync and permission failures leave document metadata uncommitted.
Corrupt and hard-linked recovery files preserve unrelated bytes and permissions.
No global umask changes in production code; the permissive umask is confined to isolated tests.
